# go test -c with several packages still compiles and links their tests once,
# and writes one copy of that binary per package, named for it. A copy
# started by its name runs its own package's tests.

go test -x -c -o $WORK/bin/ ./alpha ./beta
stderr -count=1 'link'$GOEXE' -o'
exists $WORK/bin/alpha.test$GOEXE
exists $WORK/bin/beta.test$GOEXE
exec $WORK/bin/alpha.test$GOEXE -test.v
stdout '^--- PASS: TestAlpha'
! stdout TestBeta
exec $WORK/bin/beta.test$GOEXE -test.v
stdout '^--- PASS: TestBeta'
! stdout TestAlpha

# -keepbinary writes the one binary the packages share, and the tests still
# run. Given -test.unit, it runs that package's tests. It links even when
# every result comes from the cache.
go test -x -keepbinary=$WORK/all.test$GOEXE ./alpha ./beta
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/copies/alpha'
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/copies/beta'
stderr -count=1 'link'$GOEXE' -o'
exec $WORK/all.test$GOEXE -test.unit=example.com/copies/beta -test.v
stdout '^--- PASS: TestBeta'
! stdout TestAlpha
rm $WORK/all.test$GOEXE
go test -keepbinary=$WORK/all.test$GOEXE ./alpha ./beta
stdout '^ok\s+example.com/copies/alpha\s+\(cached\)'
exists -exec $WORK/all.test$GOEXE

# Packages whose tests need two binaries cannot share one file.
! go test -keepbinary=$WORK/two.test$GOEXE ./alpha ./maxprocs
stderr 'need 2 binaries'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/copies

go 1.27
-- alpha/alpha_test.go --
package alpha

import "testing"

func TestAlpha(test *testing.T) {}
-- beta/beta_test.go --
package beta

import "testing"

func TestBeta(test *testing.T) {}
-- maxprocs/maxprocs_test.go --
//go:debug updatemaxprocs=0

package maxprocs

import "testing"

func TestMaxprocs(test *testing.T) {}
